Class PoweredUpHubRemote

java.lang.Object
io.github.jabrena.juno.api.lego.PoweredUpHubRemote
public final class PoweredUpHubRemote extends Object
A LEGO Powered Up hub (City Hub 88009, Technic Hub 88012, BOOST Move Hub 88006, DUPLO Train Hub, ...) controlled over Bluetooth Low Energy, recognized as compiler intrinsics by Juno and backed by the Arduino ArduinoBLE library (arduino-cli lib install ArduinoBLE). The board acts as a BLE central speaking the LEGO Wireless Protocol 3.0 to one hub at a time.

Ports are numbered from PORT_A; a City Hub has ports A and B, a Technic Hub and a Move Hub A to D. setMotorPower(int, int) works for every Powered Up motor (train motors, simple and tacho motors), with the power given as a percentage, -100..100.

Motors and sensors report values once enableSensor(int, int) has subscribed to one of their modes; readSensor(int) then returns the latest value the hub sent, e.g. a tacho motor's position in degrees or the button pressed on a Powered Up remote.

Works on both boards. On the UNO R4 WiFi, BLE is provided by the ESP32-S3 radio module, which cannot run BLE and Wifi at the same time. On the UNO Q, the radio belongs to the Linux side: ArduinoBLE 2.1.0 or newer tunnels raw HCI to its hci0 adapter through Arduino_RouterBridge, which needs arduino-router 0.7.0 or newer on the board.

    • PORT_TECHNIC_ACCELEROMETER

      public static final int PORT_TECHNIC_ACCELEROMETER
      The Technic Hub's (88012) built-in motion sensors, which report like a sensor on a port once enableSensor(int, int) subscribes to them: the accelerometer, the gyroscope and the tilt sensor. Each mode reports three signed 16-bit values; read them with readSensorValue(port, index, 2). The port numbers and the meaning of the values follow the community documentation of the LEGO Wireless Protocol and have not been verified on a hub.

  • Method Details

    • connect

      public static boolean connect(int timeoutMillis)
      Scans for the first advertising Powered Up hub and connects to it, returning whether a hub is connected afterwards. Waits at most timeoutMillis, or indefinitely when it is zero or negative. Returns true immediately if a hub is already connected.

    • isConnected

      public static boolean isConnected()
      Whether a hub is currently connected; turns false once the hub switches off or goes out of range.

    • hubType

      public static int hubType()
      The connected hub's TYPE_* system type id, or TYPE_UNKNOWN before connect(int).

    • setMotorPower

      public static void setMotorPower(int port, int powerPercent)
      Drives the motor on port at powerPercent of full power, -100..100 (negative runs backwards, 0 lets it coast); out-of-range values are clamped.

    • brakeMotor

      public static void brakeMotor(int port)
      Actively brakes the motor on port, unlike setMotorPower(port, 0), which lets it coast.

    • holdMotor

      public static void holdMotor(int port)
      Holds the motor on port where it is, resisting being turned: the third way to stop, next to letting it coast (setMotorPower(port, 0)) and brakeMotor(int). It sends a speed command of 0, which the hub's speed control holds, so it needs a motor with a rotation sensor. The message follows the protocol documentation; a first hands-on try suggests that it holds, but it has not been checked systematically. Any later power command releases the hold.

    • setLedColor

      public static void setLedColor(int color)
      Sets the hub's status LED to one of the COLOR_* values.

    • enableSensor

      public static void enableSensor(int port, int mode)
      Asks the hub to report every change of mode of the motor or sensor on port, for readSensor(int) to return. Mode numbers are device specific; the MODE_* constants cover common devices. Up to eight ports report at a time, and a new connect(int) starts with none, so enable them again after reconnecting.

    • readSensor

      public static int readSensor(int port)
      The latest value reported by the port enableSensor(int, int) subscribed to, or 0 before the first report. Decodes modes reporting a single 8-, 16- or 32-bit value; for a mode reporting several values (e.g. a tilt sensor's axes) only its first byte is returned. Call it regularly: values are received while it (or another hub call) runs, not during Delay.millis.

    • batteryPercent

      public static int batteryPercent()
      The hub's battery level as a percentage, 0..100, or -1 before the hub has reported it. This is the hub's own battery property, not a voltage; the first call after connect(int) subscribes to the hub's properties and waits up to 300 ms for the answers, later calls return the latest update without blocking.

    • buttonPressed

      public static boolean buttonPressed()
      Whether the hub's green button is held down right now. Subscribed on the first property call.

    • rssi

      public static int rssi()
      The Bluetooth signal strength the hub reports for this link in dBm (a negative number), or 0 if unknown.

    • firmwareVersion

      public static int firmwareVersion()
      The hub's firmware version as the protocol's packed number, or -1 if unknown; take it apart with versionMajor(int), versionMinor(int), versionBugfix(int) and versionBuild(int).

    • hardwareVersion

      public static int hardwareVersion()
      The hub's hardware version in the same packed form as firmwareVersion(), or -1 if unknown.

    • portDevice

      public static int portDevice(int port)
      The I/O device type the hub reported (Hub Attached I/O) for the external port port (PORT_A..PORT_D), one of the DEVICE_* constants or another protocol type id, or 0 if nothing is attached, the hub has not reported it yet, or port is out of range. The hub announces its ports right after connect(int) and again when something is plugged or unplugged; the announcements are received while a hub call runs, so call this regularly.

    • hubName

      public static int hubName(byte[] buffer, int capacity)
      Copies the hub's advertised name (up to 20 characters, ASCII bytes, no terminator) into buffer, at most capacity bytes, and returns how many were copied, 0 if the hub has not reported its name.

    • versionMajor

      public static int versionMajor(int version)

    • readSensorValue

      public static int readSensorValue(int port, int index, int bytesPerValue)
      The index-th value of the latest report of the port enableSensor(int, int) subscribed to, as a signed integer of bytesPerValue bytes (1, 2 or 4, little endian). For modes that report several values, such as the three axes of a motion sensor, read them one by one with index 0, 1 and 2. Returns 0 before the first report or when the report is too short for that index; see sensorReportSize(int).

    • sensorReportCount

      public static int sensorReportCount(int port)
      How many reports the hub has sent for port since enableSensor(int, int) subscribed to it, counting repeats of an unchanged value, so a program can measure how often the hub reports.

    • sensorReportSize

      public static int sensorReportSize(int port)
      How many value bytes the latest report of port carried (at most 16), 0 before the first.

    • setLedRgb

      public static void setLedRgb(int red, int green, int blue)
      Sets the hub's status LED to any colour, each channel 0..255; unlike setLedColor(int)'s 11 indexes.

    • linkMotors

      public static int linkMotors(int portA, int portB)
      Pairs the motors on ports portA and portB into one virtual port, so a single command (setLinkedMotorPower(int, int, int)) drives both in sync, as for a two-motor vehicle. The hub assigns the virtual port's number, which is returned, or -1 if the hub did not create it within 500 ms. Pairing the same two ports again returns the existing virtual port; a new connect(int) starts with none. The message formats follow the protocol documentation and have not been verified on a hub.

    • unlinkMotors

      public static void unlinkMotors(int virtualPort)
      Takes the virtual port virtualPort apart, so the two motors are driven separately again.

    • setLinkedMotorPower

      public static void setLinkedMotorPower(int virtualPort, int first, int second)
      Drives the two motors of a virtual port in one message: first for the motor on the first port given to linkMotors(int, int) and second for the other, each -100..100 (clamped), negative for backwards, 0 to coast. Mount mirrored motors with opposite signs.

    • brakeLinkedMotors

      public static void brakeLinkedMotors(int virtualPort)
      Actively brakes both motors of a virtual port.

    • batteryMillivolts

      public static int batteryMillivolts()
      The Technic Hub's supply voltage in millivolts (about 9000 with fresh batteries), or -1 if the hub has not answered. The first call subscribes to the hub's voltage sensor and waits up to 300 ms for its first report, so later calls return the latest value without blocking. The scale (a raw 0 to 4095 reading spanning 0 to 9.615 V) comes from the community protocol documentation and is not verified.

    • currentMilliamps

      public static int currentMilliamps()
      The current the Technic Hub draws, in milliamps (all motors and the hub together), or -1 if the hub has not answered; subscribed on the first call like batteryMillivolts(). Its scale (a raw 0 to 4095 reading spanning 0 to 4175 mA) is likewise unverified.

    • disconnect

      public static void disconnect()
      Closes the BLE connection, leaving the hub on and advertising again.

    • switchOff

      public static void switchOff()
      Asks the hub to switch itself off, which also ends the connection.
